limitations_and_boundaries: The dataset uses cancer cell lines and pharmacological compounds, but is intended as a broadly applicable perturbation atlas.
Differential gene expression analyses account for batch effects using DMSO-treated wells in all plates.
Three cell lines had insufficient representation and were excluded from downstream analyses.
Drug treatment and dose have a more modest effect on global transcriptomic stratification compared to cell line identity and cell cycle phase.
The authors note that findings are based on 24-hour drug treatment; longer time courses are not covered.

experiments_or_tasks: Generated a single-cell perturbation atlas of 100 million transcriptomic profiles measuring responses to 1,100 small-molecule perturbations across 50 cancer cell lines.
Performed SNP-based deconvolution to assign cells to cell line of origin.
Used Mosaic platform: cultured spheroids of mixed cell lines, treated with drugs for 24 hours, dissociated, fixed, and profiled using Parse GigaLab kit.

methods.name: Mosaic platform
methods.protocol_description: Spheroids of mixed cell lines (50 cell lines per spheroid) were cultured in suspension, treated with drug or DMSO for 24 hours, dissociated into single cells, fixed, and profiled using the Parse GigaLab scRNA-seq kit with combinatorial barcoding. Genetic variants in scRNA-seq libraries were used for SNP-based deconvolution. 14 96-well plates were processed into 1,786 sublibraries. Sequencing yielded ~1.4 trillion reads representing 153 million cells.

methods.name: scVI dimensionality reduction
methods.protocol_description: scVI was used to learn a 10-dimensional embedding for each cell. For visualization, 140,000 high-quality cells per cell line were sampled (6.58 million total) and 2-D tSNE coordinates computed.
